title: First Experiences of Last Aid Courses (LAC) in Brazil
content: Background/Objectives: Palliative Care is a key component to health care. In Brazil, the population has limited access to Palliative Care, and it remains a little-known subject. Last Aid Courses (LAC) for adults have been established since 2015 in 22 countries in Europe, Australia, America and Asia to improve the public discussion about death and dying and to empower people to participate in end-of-life care provision. In Brazil LAC started in 2020. The aim of the present study was to investigate if LACs contribute to bringing knowledge and awareness of Palliative Care to different settings in Brazil. Methods: Participants of the LAC responded to a quantitative/qualitative questionnaire provided after the course. Results: Between March and November 2024, 32 courses were offered, with 246 out of 343 participants responding to the questionnaire, showing high acceptance of the course and the most important message they take from it. Conclusions: The results of the current study indicate that the standardized approach with the normal international LAC curriculum to discuss Palliative Care and care at the end of life can be used in Brazil.
